clue.text: Carrier gets warship in an instant to withdraw

indicators.note: to withdraw is to pull back, so the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: a sub (submarine) is a warship
taken as written
a mo is a moment, an instant

explanation.surface: An aircraft carrier is joined by a warship that must pull out at a moment's notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to withdraw' turns the whole run SUBINMO backwards. 'Carrier' suggests aircraft carriers but here means a vehicle carrying passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus or coach that carries passengers was originally called by this longer name.

clue.text: Small number turn up at church no longer

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Only a small congregation shows up at church these days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' reverses NO to give ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Formerly but not now: something that was so in former times is no longer so.

clue.text: He ruled in pre-Antonine Rome

indicators.note: in signals the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A historical note that a certain emperor reigned before the Antonine dynasty.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the end of 'pre-Antonine' and the start of 'Rome'. Fittingly, this emperor did rule Rome before the Antonines.
explanation.definitionFit: This Roman emperor was a ruler, so a description of a man who ruled fits him.

clue.text: Squander one's stake in an investment

parts.note: to blue money is to squander it (old British slang)
a chip is a gambler's stake at the table

explanation.surface: Advice not to waste your money by gambling it on a share purchase.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'blue' money is old British slang for spending it recklessly.
explanation.definitionFit: A share in a large, reliable company is called by this term, from the highest-value poker counter.

clue.text: Quick trim

definitions.meaning: ... can mean brisk, as in a ... pace

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both brisk in pace and neat in appearance, two separate senses.

clue.text: Throws away fights?

definitions.meaning: discards, gets rid of as useless

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means discards, and the plural noun means brawls in informal speech.

clue.text: Exults with a number in throngs

indicators.note: in places the number inside the word for exults

parts.note: to crow is to exult, boastfully
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: People rejoice along with many others in the crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: Large packed masses of people are synonyms for throngs.

clue.text: It's put in by an attendant

definitions.text: It's put in by an attendant

parts.words: It's put in by an attendant
parts.note: an attendant here is anyone who attends, and what they put in is their presence

explanation.definitionFit: Someone attending an event is said to put in this, meaning they show up.

clue.text: Gets quickly to one's feet, but doesn't make a move

definitions.meaning: holds firm and refuses to budge

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase is rising swiftly; as an idiom it means holding one's ground.

clue.text: High time many received an awakening

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, a crossword way to say many
arousal is an awakening

explanation.surface: It was about time a lot of people were stirred into action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High time' looks like 'it is about time' but means a riotous drinking party.
explanation.definitionFit: A drunken revel is a high old time, a spree of merrymaking.

clue.text: A fair game

parts.note: not a game played fairly but a game found at a funfair, throwing rings over prizes

explanation.definitionFit: This ring-tossing stall is a classic sideshow at a funfair.

clue.text: Heavenly body became a model on a vase

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: an artist's model sits, so sat means posed
an urn is a vase

explanation.surface: A celestial figure was painted posing on a Grecian vase.
explanation.definitionFit: This ringed planet is a heavenly body in the solar system.

clue.text: The Met Office?

parts.note: not the weather service but the office of the Met, the London Metropolitan Police

explanation.definitionFit: The headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police is known by this name.

clue.text: Very important events, by the way

definitions.meaning: markers set beside a road showing distances

explanation.definitionFit: Literally stone markers along a road; figuratively key moments in a story.

clue.text: Turn on physician, one likely to misrepresent account

parts.note: a spin is a turn
a physician is a doctor

explanation.surface: A patient rounds on a doctor, suspecting a false account of events.
explanation.definitionFit: A political publicist who puts a favourable slant on events is so called.

clue.text: I am easily shocked at city giving licence to print

parts.note: I'm is short for I am
prim means prudish, easily shocked
taken as written
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to being prudish about a town that grants printing licences.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'let it be printed', the official approval to publish a book.

clue.text: A school loses business claim

indicators.note: loses means the business letters are taken out of the school

parts.note: a college is a school
CO is short for company, a business

explanation.surface: An academy goes out of business and files a legal claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' removes CO from COLLEGE, leaving LLEGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert something without proof is to claim it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: He gets red if strangers address him

definitions.text: He gets red if strangers address him

parts.words: He gets red if strangers address him
parts.note: this short name is used by friends; strangers would use the full formal form, which adds the letters of red on the end

explanation.definitionFit: This is the familiar short form of a man's name that becomes Alfred in full.

clue.text: General resemblance to Humpty Dumpty?

definitions.meaning: versatile, comprehensive, as in a general athlete
Humpty Dumpty, the nursery rhyme egg, is round on every side

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means versatile or comprehensive, and literally describes an egg-shaped figure.

clue.text: Time one changed

indicators.note: changed means the letters of one are rearranged

explanation.surface: Time makes one a different person.
explanation.definitionFit: An immense age is a period of time, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Pirate captain bolts, seeing firearms

parts.note: Captain Flint is the pirate in Stevenson's Treasure Island
bolts on doors are locks

explanation.surface: A pirate captain runs off on spotting guns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bolts' looks like a verb (runs away) but is a noun for door fastenings.
explanation.definitionFit: Old muskets and pistols fired by a flint striking steel were called this.

clue.text: Devastating winger

parts.note: not a footballer on the wing but a winged insect whose swarms devastate crops

explanation.definitionFit: This swarming grasshopper flies on wings and strips crops bare.

clue.text: Complete meal for the road

parts.note: thorough means complete, utter
fare is food, a meal

explanation.surface: A full meal provided for a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A main road or public street through a place is a synonym for road.

clue.text: Popular craze takes me in

indicators.note: takes, together with in, says the craze holds the next word inside it
in completes the instruction that me goes inside the craze

parts.note: a fad is a craze
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fashionable fad has drawn me in.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well known and celebrated is close to being popular.

clue.text: Second generation savant

parts.note: an age is a generation, a period

explanation.surface: A scholar from the next generation of thinkers.
explanation.definitionFit: A wise and learned person is a sage, synonym for savant.

clue.text: Inadequate tip?

explanation.definitionFit: The word means meagre as an adjective and to tilt as a verb.

clue.text: At home with the bowling, apparently

definitions.text: At home with the bowling, apparently

parts.words: At home with the bowling, apparently
parts.note: in cricket a batsman still in, at home at the crease, has survived the bowling

explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a batsman who has not been dismissed is described this way, still in.

clue.text: Go for a stroll, but with a meal out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Going for a walk, but having lunch out on the way.
explanation.definitionFit: The formal verb means to walk about, which is going for a stroll.

clue.text: Odd start to A levels

indicators.note: odd marks the letters as strange, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange beginning to a student's A level exams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A levels' are British school-leaving exams; the A is fodder, 'levels' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Geological layers of rock are levels lying one above another.

clue.text: Resentment shown when a failure has gone astray

parts.note: a dud is a failure

indicators.note: gone astray means the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A grudge held because a dud product has gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep indignation or a fit of pique, as in high dudgeon, is resentment.
